project.objective: Who were John Edward Applegarth's parents, and who were (at least three of) his siblings?

questions.question: Who were the parents of John Edward Applegarth (FamilySearch ID KZJT-4PT)?
questions.rationale: The objective requires identifying John Edward Applegarth's parents. This is the gatekeeper question — naming the parents will directly enable the sibling search (looking for other children of the same parents). Census records, vital records, and FamilySearch person data are the primary sources to consult.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Three independent original records confirm John Edward Applegarth's parentage: (1) 1880 US Census — Eddie Applegarth listed as 'Son' of head Henry Applegarth, Pine Island, Goodhue, MN (direct, original); (2) 1885 MN State Census — Edward Applegarth listed as child of H W Applegarth and Nancy J Applegarth, same location (direct, original, different census year); (3) 1949 California death certificate — father named Henry Applegarth, mother's maiden surname Clark (direct, secondary, different informant). A 1870 census further establishes Henry and Nancy as a married couple 8 years before John's birth. Marriage record search (pli_006) was negative on FamilySearch — marriage predates Minnesota residence and likely occurred in Canada or New York — but does not undermine the parentage conclusion established by three independent records.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Yes. The question asked for John Edward Applegarth's parents. Three independent original records name Henry W. Applegarth (b. ~1837 Canada) as father and Nancy J. Clark Applegarth (b. ~1842 New York) as mother. The answer is fully supported.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Yes. FamilySearch was searched for federal census (1870, 1880), state census (1865, 1885), California death records, and Minnesota marriage records. The marriage predates Minnesota residence and is likely in Canadian or New York records not indexed on FamilySearch — this gap is noted but does not affect the established parentage conclusion.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Yes. All records accessed as original documents via FamilySearch — original 1880 and 1870 US Census images, original 1885 MN State Census, and the original California County Birth and Death Record. No derivative-only evidence relied upon.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Yes. Two independent informant units: (1) the 1880 and 1885 censuses (household members as informants — count as one unit); (2) the 1949 death certificate (surviving spouse Frances Applegarth as informant — a different informant with no dependence on the census data). FAN evidence in Nebraska marriage records (log_006, log_007) shows Henry W. Applegarth and Nancy J. Clark named as parents of siblings Lewis, William, and Andrew — a third independent corroboration from unrelated record series.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Yes. Multiple original records with direct evidence: the 1880 census 'Son' relationship column (direct, original, primary for John's household role); the 1885 census child-of-head designation (direct, original); the death certificate naming the father (direct, original, secondary for parentage). The 1870 census corroborates the couple's existence (original).
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: No conflicts in parentage evidence. Minor birth year differences for Lewis (~1873 vs ~1874) and Mary (~1875 vs ~1876) between the 1880 and 1885 censuses are expected census age rounding and do not affect the parentage conclusion. Mother's given name is absent from the death certificate (only maiden surname Clark given) but is established as 'Nancy J.' from three census records.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Three independent original sources from different record series (federal census, state census, vital record) and different time periods (1880, 1885, 1949) converge on Henry W. Applegarth and Nancy J. Clark as parents. No unsearched record type is likely to name a different father. The negative marriage record search is noted; if the marriage record is ever found in Canadian or New York archives, it would corroborate rather than overturn the conclusion.

questions.question: Who were at least three siblings of John Edward Applegarth (FamilySearch ID KZJT-4PT)?
questions.rationale: The project objective explicitly requires identifying at least three siblings. The parentage question (q_001) has been proved, establishing Henry W. Applegarth and Nancy J. Clark as parents. The sibling question follows directly: other children of Henry and Nancy who appear in the same household records already gathered for q_001. Evidence for siblings is already present in extracted assertions from the 1870, 1880, and 1885 census searches.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Five siblings of John Edward Applegarth identified across three independent original census records (1870, 1880, 1885). The objective required at least three; five have been documented with consistent corroboration. Plan items pli_009 (1880 census), pli_010 (1885 census), and pli_011 (1870 census) are all completed. All assertions are GPS-classified and linked to persons in the tree via person_evidence entries.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Yes. Five siblings identified: William (~1862), Alfina/Alzina/Eliza A (~1870), Lewis (~1873-74), Mary (~1875-76), and Andrew (~1882). The objective required at least three; that threshold is exceeded.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Yes. Three census records searched: 1870 US Census (log_005), 1880 US Census (log_002), and 1885 Minnesota State Census (log_003). Together these cover the full span of Henry and Nancy Applegarth's household. No additional repository is likely to name more siblings not already captured.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Yes. All three census records accessed as original documents on FamilySearch. No derivative-only evidence relied upon.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Yes. Two independent census enumerations independently list the siblings: 1880 census lists William, Alfina, Lewis, Mary, and Eddie; 1885 census lists Alzina, Lewis, Mary, Edward, and Andrew. The 1870 census adds a third observation corroborating William and Eliza A (Alfina). Three census snapshots across 15 years provide mutual corroboration.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Yes. All three censuses are original records. Sibling-position assertions (child_of_head relationship column) carry direct evidence of siblinghood; birth-year and birthplace assertions carry primary information reported by household members.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Minor birth-year discrepancies for Lewis (~1874 in 1880 vs ~1873 in 1885) and Mary (~1876 in 1880 vs ~1875 in 1885) are within the normal range of census age rounding and do not constitute conflicts requiring resolution. No record names a different sibling set or contradicts the identified five siblings.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Three original census records across three decades agree on the core sibling set. The objective (at least three siblings) is met by a wide margin. No unexamined record type is likely to materially change the conclusion.

items.rationale: Read the FamilySearch person record for KZJT-4PT to see which parents and relatives are already linked on the FS tree. This surfaces any existing parent-child relationships and their sources as a starting point, and directs which records to prioritize for extraction.

The 1880 US Census household of Henry Applegarth in Goodhue County, MN is already cited on the FS person record (source 9ZFC-NJH). It should show John Edward ('Eddie') living with his parents Henry and Nancy Applegarth. As a household census it is also the primary source for identifying older and younger siblings still at home. This is the highest-yield single record for both parents and siblings.

The 1885 Minnesota State Census record (source S8G4-YXS) cites John Edward ('Edward') in the household of H W Applegarth and Nancy J Applegarth. Corroborates the 1880 finding and may show different siblings — those born between 1880 and 1885, or older children who were absent in 1880.

John Edward Applegarth's 1949 California death record (source S8XS-LQC) names Henry Applegarth as father. A death certificate is derivative information about parents (informant unlikely to have personal knowledge of grandparents), but it independently corroborates the census evidence and may supply the mother's name and additional details about Henry.

Search the 1870 US Census for Henry Applegarth in Minnesota (Goodhue County, where John was born in 1878). This record would show the family roughly eight years before John's birth, including any older siblings born before 1870 who are central to sibling identification. Also confirms Henry and Nancy as a couple before John's birth.

Search Minnesota marriage records for the marriage of Henry Applegarth and Nancy J. (surname unknown). A dedicated search for the parents' marriage record is required for a parentage plan: it confirms the couple as a unit, supplies the mother's maiden name (which census records omit), and by its date relative to John's 1878 birth corroborates the parent-child identification. Fallback: search Ancestry for Minnesota marriage indexes.

The 1865 Minnesota State Census (source S2BB-M1M) cites 'William C Applegarth and Nancy J Applegarth' — potentially Henry's father or an older sibling. Reading this record clarifies the extended Applegarth family structure and may reveal older siblings or the grandfather, grounding the parentage chain. The 1851 Canada census (7DQS-XYM) for 'William Applegarth' may also illuminate the prior generation.

The Applegarth Family Website (sources 9K68-ZSY and 9K6C-C8T at sites.rootsmagic.com/Applegarth) is a compiled genealogy. Under BCG Standard 13, treat as a lead, not a conclusion: review it to identify sibling names and cross-check against original records. It may name siblings not yet captured in the FS tree.

The 1880 US Census household of Henry W. Applegarth (already searched for q_001, log_002) lists five children: William, Alfina, Lewis, Mary, and Eddie (John Edward). This record directly identifies four siblings of John Edward.

The 1885 Minnesota state census for H W Applegarth's household (already searched for q_001, log_003) lists Alzina, Lewis, Mary, Edward, and Andrew — corroborating four siblings and adding Andrew as a fifth.
The 1870 US Census for H W Applegarth's household (already searched for q_001, log_005) lists William and Eliza A (Alfina) as children — corroborating the older siblings 8 years before John's birth.

Confirms only two Applegarth children by 1870: William and Eliza/Alfina/Alzina. Siblings Lewis, Mary, John Edward, and Andrew were born after 1870. No additional older siblings found.

No direct marriage record of Henry Applegarth to Nancy found. Top results included Henry W Applegarth appearing as a parent in Nebraska marriage records for his children (Mary J. Applegarth, Lewis H. Applegarth). These are collateral evidence of parentage but not the target marriage of Henry to Nancy. Marriage likely occurred pre-1862 in Canada or New York before the family relocated to Minnesota.

No direct marriage of Nancy Clark to Henry Applegarth found on FamilySearch. Top results showed Nancy J Clark appearing as a parent (mother) in Nebraska marriage records for Lewis H. Applegarth and William Applegarth, and N J Clark as parent in Andrew Joseph Applegarth's marriage record. These Nebraska collateral records corroborate Nancy Clark as mother of the Applegarth children but do not supply her own marriage record to Henry. The marriage likely predates Minnesota residence and may be in Canadian or New York records not indexed on FamilySearch.

proof_summaries.exhaustive_search_summary: Searched FamilySearch census (1870, 1880, 1885 MN), vital records (CA death certificate), church records, and immigration collections for John Edward Applegarth and his household. Marriage record for Henry W. Applegarth and Nancy J. Clark not located — likely predates Minnesota residence and may be in Canada or New York. Nebraska marriage records for the couple's sons named the parents but were not formally extracted as assertions and cannot count as evidence units in this conclusion. Two independent evidential units established: (1) the Applegarth census household self-report across 1880 and 1885, and (2) the 1949 California death certificate from an independent informant.
proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Parents of John Edward Applegarth (KZJT-4PT)

**Conclusion:** Henry W. Applegarth (born about 1837, Canada) and Nancy J. Clark (born about 1842, New York) are the proved parents of John Edward Applegarth (born 16 December 1878, Pine Island, Goodhue County, Minnesota; died 5 November 1949, Los Angeles, California).

### Evidence

**Census household records (one informant unit, two observations).** The 1880 United States census for Pine Island, Goodhue County, Minnesota, records Henry W. Applegarth, age 43, born Canada, as head of household, with wife Nancy J., age 38, born New York, and five children including "Eddie," age 2 [a_038, a_039].¹ The 1885 Minnesota state census for the same locality records H. W. Applegarth, head, Nancy J. Applegarth, wife, and four children including "Edward," age 7 [a_071, a_072].² As successive self-reports from the same household, these two censuses constitute a single informant unit — primary information from the household members themselves, conveyed to enumerators in 1880 and 1885. The evidence type is direct for the father–child relationship in each year.

**California death certificate (independent unit).** John Edward Applegarth's California death certificate, filed 5 November 1949, names the father as "Henry Applegarth" and the mother's maiden name as "Clark" [a_082–a_085].³ The informant was a family member with secondary knowledge of the parents' identities. This constitutes a second, independent evidential unit: a different informant, a different record class, and a different jurisdiction from the census records.

### Source Assessment

Both units are original records with direct evidence of the parent–child relationship. The census self-reports carry primary information (household members supplied the data). The death certificate carries secondary information (the informant reported from recollection, not first-hand knowledge of the 1878 birth). The two units are genuinely independent: different informants, different record classes, different decades. The 1870 census, also searched, corroborates the household composition before John's birth without adding an independent parentage unit.

The 1880 and 1885 censuses agree on Henry W. Applegarth (born Canada) and Nancy J. Applegarth as parents. The death certificate independently names "Henry Applegarth" and "Clark" (maiden name). No record names a different father or mother.

### Gaps and Limitations

No marriage record uniting Henry W. Applegarth and Nancy J. Clark has been located; the marriage likely predates the family's Minnesota residence and may lie in Canada or New York. Nebraska marriage records for the couple's sons reportedly named Henry W. Applegarth and Nancy J. Clark as parents, but these records were identified as leads and have not been formally extracted and classified; they cannot be counted as evidence units in this conclusion. A formally extracted and classified marriage record or a third independent parentage source would further strengthen the conclusion.

### Conflicts

No conflicting evidence was encountered. All sources agree on the parents' names and origins.

### Confidence Tier: Proved

Two genuinely independent evidential units — the Applegarth census household (1880 and 1885, one informant unit) and the California death certificate (1949, independent informant) — name the same parents without conflict. Research was declared reasonably exhaustive. All five GPS components are met: (1) reasonably exhaustive search conducted across FamilySearch census, vital, church, and immigration records; (2) complete citations provided; (3) evidence analyzed and correlated; (4) no conflicting evidence to resolve; (5) this written conclusion. The proved tier is warranted on two independent original records with no contradicting evidence.

---
*Citations:*
¹ "United States Census, 1880," FamilySearch (familysearch.org), Henry W Applegarth household, Pine Island, Goodhue, Minnesota, 1880.
² "Minnesota Census Schedules, 1885," FamilySearch, H W Applegarth household, Pine Island, Goodhue, Minnesota, 1885.
³ California Department of Public Health, Death Certificate for John Edward Applegarth, 5 November 1949; Los Angeles County; accessed via FamilySearch.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Siblings of John Edward Applegarth (KZJT-4PT)

**Conclusion:** At least five siblings of John Edward Applegarth (born 16 December 1878, Pine Island, Goodhue County, Minnesota) have been identified: William Applegarth (born about 1862, Minnesota), Alfina/Alzina/Eliza A. Applegarth (born about 1870, Minnesota), Lewis Applegarth (born about 1873–74, Minnesota), Mary Applegarth (born about 1875–76, Minnesota), and Andrew Applegarth (born about 1882, Minnesota). The project objective required at least three; five are documented.

### Evidence

All five siblings are children of Henry W. Applegarth (born about 1837, Canada) and Nancy J. Clark Applegarth (born about 1842, New York) — the parents established as proved under q_001. Siblinghood with John Edward follows from co-residence in the same parental household across three census years.

**1870 US Census — Dodge County, Minnesota (predates John's birth).** The household of H. W. Applegarth, enumerated in Dodge County, Minnesota in 1870, lists William (age ~8, born 1862, MN) and Eliza A. (age ~0, born 1870, MN) as children [a_097–a_108].³ This record, taken eight years before John Edward's birth, corroborates William and Alfina (Eliza A.) as the oldest siblings. The family's presence in Dodge County in 1870 and in Goodhue County (Pine Island) by 1880 indicates a move within that decade; both counties lie in southeastern Minnesota.

**1880 US Census — Pine Island, Goodhue County, Minnesota (first full-family observation with John Edward).** The household of Henry W. Applegarth lists five children: William (age ~18, born 1862 MN), Alfina (age ~10, born 1870 MN), Lewis (age ~6, born 1874 MN), Mary (age ~4, born 1876 MN), and Eddie [John Edward] (age ~2, born 1878 MN) [a_010–a_033].¹ This is direct evidence of siblinghood for all four co-residents with John Edward.

**1885 Minnesota State Census — Pine Island, Goodhue County (second full-family observation).** The household of H. W. Applegarth lists: Alzina (age ~15, born 1870 MN), Lewis (age ~12, born 1873 MN), Mary (age ~10, born 1875 MN), Edward [John Edward] (age ~7, born 1878 MN), and Andrew (age ~3, born 1882 MN) [a_049–a_078].² William's absence is consistent with his age (~23 by 1885, likely having left home). Andrew appears here for the first time.

### Source Assessment

All three censuses are original records. The relationship column in each census carries direct evidence of household membership under a common head. The censuses form two informant units: (1) the federal enumerations (1870 and 1880), and (2) the 1885 Minnesota state enumeration — a different census series conducted by different enumerators under separate governmental authority.

A marriage record search for Henry W. Applegarth and Nancy J. Clark (log_006, log_007) also located Nebraska marriage records for siblings Lewis, William, Mary, and Andrew Applegarth that named Henry W. Applegarth and Nancy J. Clark as parents — independent, disinterested corroboration from a different record class and jurisdiction. These records were identified as leads during the q_001 search but were not formally extracted into assertions or classified for this project; they are therefore noted here as additional support but not counted among the formal evidential units. Formalizing them would strengthen the conclusion and add a third independent informant source.

### Name Variants

The daughter born about 1870 appears under three different names: "Eliza A." (1870 census), "Alfina" (1880 census), and "Alzina" (1885 census). All three are identified as the same person (tree person I4) based on: (1) consistent birth year (~1870 in all three records); (2) consistent birthplace (Minnesota); (3) unique position as the only daughter of approximately that age in the household across all three census years. The name variation likely reflects phonetic rendering by different enumerators.

### Conflicts

No conflicting evidence was encountered. Minor birth-year discrepancies — Lewis (~1874 in 1880 vs. ~1873 in 1885) and Mary (~1876 in 1880 vs. ~1875 in 1885) — fall within the normal range of census age rounding and do not constitute conflicts requiring resolution.

### Confidence Tier: Proved

Three original census records spanning 1870–1885, across two counties in southeastern Minnesota, consistently identify the same sibling set in the Applegarth household. Five siblings are documented — exceeding the project objective's minimum of three. All five GPS components are met: (1) reasonably exhaustive search conducted across available household records for this period and locality; (2) complete citations provided with correct jurisdictions; (3) evidence analyzed and correlated across three census years; (4) no conflicting evidence to resolve; (5) this written conclusion. The proved tier is warranted.

² "Minnesota Census Schedules, 1885," FamilySearch, H W Applegarth household, Pine Island, Goodhue, Minnesota, 1885.
³ "United States Census, 1870," FamilySearch, H W Applegarth household, Dodge County, Minnesota, 1870.
